subject: general
question: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kampili**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The founders of the Vijayanagar Empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya, were originally ministers in the kingdom of **Kampili**.
 
• Kampili was a small but strategically significant kingdom located in present-day Karnataka.
 
• The kingdom of Kampili resisted invasions by the Delhi Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the early 14th century.
 
• After the fall of Kampili to the Delhi Sultanate, Harihara and Bukka were captured and reportedly converted to Islam but later reconverted to Hinduism by the sage Vidyaranya.
 
• Inspired by Vidyaranya, Harihara and Bukka went on to establish the Vijayanagar Empire in 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kampili Kingdom:**

 
 
• Kampili was ruled by King Kampiladeva, who resisted the Delhi Sultanate's invasions with great valor but was eventually defeated.
 
• The kingdom's fall marked a turning point in South Indian history, leading to the rise of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
 
 
• **Vidyaranya:**
 
 
• Vidyaranya was a prominent Hindu saint and scholar who played a crucial role in the establishment of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
• He served as the spiritual advisor to Harihara and Bukka and worked to revive Hindu culture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Vijayanagar Empire:**
 
 
• Founded in 1336 CE by Harihara and Bukka, the Vijayanagar Empire became one of the most powerful South Indian empires.
 
• The empire was known for its advancements in art, architecture, and administration, with Hampi as its capital.
 
• It reached its zenith during the reign of Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE).
 
 
 
• **Battle of Talikota:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire fell after its defeat in the Battle of Talikota in 1565 CE against the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates.
 
• Despite its fall, the empire's cultural and historical legacy continues to influence South India.
